era_results.narrator_text: I was born on December 31, 1960, in West St. Paul, Minnesota. My mother is still alive at 99 and lives in St. Paul, so those earliest roots are still connected to my life now.
era_results.lori_response: West St. Paul and St. Paul — those roots in Minnesota are still strong. What do you remember about your early years in Minnesota, particularly around the winter holidays when you were a baby?

era_results.narrator_text: I went to school in St. Paul. I also attended military school, but that was school, not military service. I did not serve in the military.
era_results.lori_response: St. Paul again, where you went to school. What does "military school" bring to mind for you, aside from the distinction you made about not serving in the military?

era_results.narrator_text: When I was a teenager, my father died. He was changing a tire and was hit by a car. I also traveled in Europe as a teenager.
era_results.lori_response: Europe. What are some memories that have stayed with you from that trip?

era_results.narrator_text: I went to college in New York. I earned one bachelor's degree and three master's degrees. I do not want to fill in the school names or majors right now.
era_results.lori_response: New York. What do you remember about your time in New York during that period?

era_results.narrator_text: My work life included selling natural tobacco cigarettes and being a beer maker or brewer. Later I taught at NMHU, New Mexico Highlands University. I became a school psychologist in 2010.
era_results.lori_response: NMHU, that's where you taught. What does it mean to you that you transitioned to becoming a school psychologist in 2010, and what motivated you to take on that role? (We can come back to the rest in a moment.)

era_results.narrator_text: I have been married twice. I am divorced again now. I have two children. I continued my professional identity as a school psychologist in New Mexico.
era_results.lori_response: We've touched on several parts of your story. Where would you like to continue today?

era_results.narrator_text: Today I live alone in my own house in Las Vegas, New Mexico. I currently work as a school psychologist in Pecos Schools. My mother is still alive at 99 and lives in St. Paul.
era_results.lori_response: Las Vegas, New Mexico, and your work in Pecos Schools. Your mother's longevity and connection to her hometown in Minnesota are remarkable. What does life in Las Vegas feel like for you now?
